submodules.contenido:
Evil isn't a product of our freedom, but the **concealment of the essence of things**, of their light.

*Evil is when something good doesn't occupy the place that belongs to it.*

*The energies of the Tree are neutral.*

Evil appears when the masculine and the feminine energy, instead of uniting, confront each other in one of the dimensions of the **Tree of Life**, which structures the human soul.

Will quickly turns into stubbornness when it isn't used correctly.

*The negative side appears when strength isn't put to work toward a concrete goal and we move forward blindly, without using intelligence.*

---

*I can only be bad if there's something inside me that predisposes me to it.*

External forces find it easier to influence us wherever there are aspects of ourselves we don't yet understand or integrate.

**Amalek** is the denial of spirituality; it's believing yourself separate.

Amalek denies the existence of other dimensions: it exists in **Malkhut** and doesn't believe in spirituality, only in good and evil.

It always ends up destroying itself; its essence is the unconsciousness of believing itself disconnected from the infinite.

*Evil always takes its own life.*

In Judaism, **ha-Satan** means *"the adversary"* or *"the accuser"* (not the devil of Christianity).

He appears in the Book of Job as an agent who **acts with divine permission in order to put the human being to the test.**

Through Satan, the soul experiences **lack**, **desire**, **fear** and **ego**, which is what makes human experience and human freedom possible.

His function is to hide the light, generate obstacles, produce doubts and create the illusion of separation.

*Without resistance there would be no revelation.*

Only through **Da'at** and consciousness can the light emerge.

*He is the engineer of the soul's evolution.*

---

He shows up above all in **Malkhut** in the form of **fear**, **anxiety**, **procrastination** and **the need for control**.

These manifestations serve to test the **kli**, to reveal its limits and to show where it's fragmented.

*External forces find it easier to influence us wherever there is still unconsciousness or fragmentation.*

opciones: A) The human being misuses their freedom.
B) The light is concealed and the energies fall out of alignment.
C) Satan acts without divine permission.
ejercicios.enunciado: According to the text, evil arises mainly when:

opciones: A) A positive capacity used outside its proper place.
B) An unpleasant emotion.
C) An action that society considers wrong.
ejercicios.enunciado: Which of these situations best fits the definition of evil proposed here?

opciones: A) No energy is good or bad in itself.
B) Good and evil are illusions.
C) The Sefirot have no influence on human behavior.
ejercicios.enunciado: The phrase "the energies of the Tree are neutral" implies that:

opciones: A) A healthy expression of Gevurah.
B) A positive energy used in an unbalanced way.
C) An influence coming solely from Satan.
ejercicios.enunciado: An extremely disciplined person ends up becoming rigid, obsessive and unable to adapt. According to the text, this would be:

opciones: A) Because they're stronger than human will.
B) Because there are inner areas that are still unconscious or fragmented.
C) Because matter always rules over spirit.
ejercicios.enunciado: Why do external forces find it easier to influence a person?

opciones: A) A demonic entity independent of God.
B) The tendency to believe we're separate from the infinite.
C) The punishment for acting wrongly.
ejercicios.enunciado: What does Amalek represent in this course?

opciones: A) Satan acts within the divine order and fulfills a function.
B) Satan doesn't really exist.
C) Satan represents negative emotions and nothing else.
ejercicios.enunciado: According to the description given, what is the main difference between Satan and the Christian devil?

opciones: A) To punish human mistakes.
B) To prevent spiritual evolution.
C) To create resistance so that consciousness can develop.
ejercicios.enunciado: What is the deepest function of the obstacles Satan generates?

opciones: A) A fragmented Malkhut.
B) An excessive Chokhmah.
C) A balanced Tiferet.
ejercicios.enunciado: Someone tries to control absolutely everything because they live in constant fear of uncertainty. According to the text, this would mainly be a manifestation of:

opciones: A) Evil is an independent force that fights against God.
B) Evil is an absence of consciousness and of connection with the light.
C) Evil is simply the result of making bad decisions.
ejercicios.enunciado: Which of these sentences best sums up the view of evil presented here?
